chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God have mercy upon him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdul Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi, who said:

I went to the door of the house in Sarakhs in which Ar-Rida' was imprisoned and he was bound there. I asked the prison guard for permission to visit him. He said, 'There is no way for you to reach him.' I asked, 'Why?' He said, 'Because he may pray one thousand units of prayer in his day and night. He only stops from his prayer for an hour in the early part of the day, before midday, and at the time of the yellowing of the sun. He is in these times sitting in his place of prayer, conversing with his Lord.' I said, 'Then seek permission for me during these times.' He sought permission for me, and I entered upon him while he was sitting in his place of prayer, thinking.

I said, 'O son of God's Prophet! What is this that the people narrate about you?' He said, 'What is it?' I said, 'They say that you claim that the people are your slaves.' He said, 'O God! Creator of the heavens and the Earth, Knower of the unseen and the visible, You are witness that I have never said that I have never said that, nor did I hear any of my forefathers (peace be upon them) say it. And You are the Knower of the oppressions imposed upon us by this nation, and that this is one of them.'
Then he turned to me and said, 'O Abdul Salam! If all the people are our slaves as they narrate about us, then from whom do we buy them?' I said, 'O son of God's Prophet! You are truthful.'

Then he said, 'O Abdul Salam! Do you deny what God, the Mighty and Majestic, has made incumbent upon us regarding the Wilayah (Guardianship/Authority), as others deny it?' I said, 'Far be it from God! No, I bear witness to your Wilayah.'

key_terms.الرِّضَاءُ: Ar-Rida', title of the eighth Imam
key_terms.بِسَرَخْسَ: In Sarakhs, a city in Khurasan

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Imams claiming people are their slaves according to Imam Ar-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights Imam al-Rida’s (a.s.) profound devotion, noting his practice of praying a thousand rak'ahs daily, which underscores the spiritual depth expected of the Imam. When addressing the popular claim that the Imams consider people their 'slaves,' he clarifies it as a misunderstanding of their divine *Wilayah* (authority) rather than literal ownership, using a logical rhetorical question to refute the literal interpretation. The Imam then pivots to affirm the core Shia doctrine of *Wilayah*, asking Abdul Salam if he denies the authority God established for them, to which the visitor affirms, linking their status to divine decree rather than human subjugation.
